pillars.name: Digital Inclusion
pillars.outcome: Digital skills, assistive devices and mentorship that connect rural youth, women and persons with disabilities to the digital economy.
pillars.lead: We work to close Kenya's digital divide where it is widest, equipping youth, women and persons with disabilities with the skills, tools and mentorship to build real solutions and thrive in a connected economy.
overview: Digital Inclusion is a central driver of the Foundation's mission. It focuses on widening access to digital tools, skills and innovation so that opportunity no longer depends on where a person lives, with particular attention to youth and persons with disabilities.
We treat technology as a means rather than an end. It belongs wherever it improves outcomes people care about: finding work, running a business, continuing to learn, or communicating independently.
focus: Digital literacy and online-work skills for youth and women
Assistive technology for persons with disabilities, with training on its use
Mentorship from people already working in the digital economy
Tech hubs and training materials designed for rural learners

programmes.title: Digital skills and mentorship
programmes.text: Practical training in digital literacy, online work and online safety, paired with mentors who show what is possible.

programmes.title: Assistive devices
programmes.text: Screen readers, adaptive keyboards and specialised software, procured with specialist institutions and backed by training so they are used well.

programmes.title: Community tech hubs
programmes.text: Shared spaces with devices and connectivity where young people can learn, practise and take on online work close to home.

help.donate: Fund tech hubs, assistive devices and training materials tailored to rural learners.
help.volunteer: Mentor learners, teach digital skills or support community outreach.
help.partner: Corporate and education partners strengthen delivery; sponsorship schemes can support a whole cohort of learners.

pillars.name: Education & Leadership
pillars.outcome: French lessons for 570 students in five Kirinyaga schools, alongside school libraries and leadership mentoring.
pillars.lead: We champion inclusive education that unlocks potential, nurtures curiosity and connects learners to a wider world, and we cultivate young leaders who will drive change in their own communities.
overview: Education & Leadership focuses on closing learning gaps and developing leaders who inspire social change. By including youth, women and persons with disabilities from the start, we strengthen the base for lasting community growth.

Our flagship programme, the French Initiative, began in August 2025 with five schools in Kirinyaga County. It gives 570 students a second international language and, with it, a wider choice of studies and careers.
focus: Language learning as a gateway to regional and global opportunity
School libraries that give every learner access to books
Mentorship and leadership development for young people
Inclusive learning for students with disabilities

programmes.title: The French Initiative
programmes.text: Weekly French classes, clubs and cultural activities in five Kirinyaga schools, reaching 570 students, many of whom had never studied a foreign language.

programmes.title: School libraries
programmes.text: Working with schools to establish libraries within their compounds, giving hundreds of students inclusive access to books and quiet places to learn.

programmes.title: Leadership development
programmes.text: Mentorship and leadership opportunities that prepare young people, especially young women, to lead in their schools and communities.

help.donate: Support scholarships, French instruction, learning materials and library development.
help.volunteer: Join as a mentor, French language instructor or literacy coach.
help.partner: Schools can host programmes; companies can sponsor leadership and capacity-building work.

pillars.name: Women's Economic Empowerment
pillars.outcome: Skills, networks and market access for women entrepreneurs and smallholder farmers, from Kiine Ward to the national stage.
pillars.lead: We equip women, youth and smallholder farmers with the skills, resources and networks to build livelihoods that last, with dignity and independence.
overview: This pillar starts from a simple belief: every Kenyan deserves a fair chance to thrive. We work through practical, locally anchored initiatives with women, youth, persons with disabilities and smallholder farmers.

In October 2026 the Foundation took 42 livestock, poultry, coffee and tea farmers from Kiine Ward, Kirinyaga County, to the Agriculture and Food Systems Transformation Summit in Nairobi, so that the people who grow Kenya's food were in the room where its future was being discussed.
focus: Entrepreneurship and financial skills for women
Farmer training built around demonstration plots
Digital tools and market linkages for small enterprises
Bringing rural producers into national conversations

pillars.name: Wellness
pillars.outcome: Monthly mental-health forums that equip people to hold supportive conversations and find the right help.
pillars.lead: We promote mental wellness by creating safe, supportive spaces where people can speak, share and grow, because strong minds build strong communities.
overview: Neither a strong economy nor good education can thrive without healthy people. Our Wellness pillar works where physical and mental health meet, with a present focus on mental health.

Each month we hold an online forum with partner service providers. Participants learn how to hold a supportive conversation and how to encourage professional help or self-help, much as a first aider would for a physical injury. The aim is to reduce stigma and offer first-level care. Early feedback has been warmly appreciative, and it encourages us to continue preventative, dignity-affirming support.
focus: Mental-health awareness and stigma reduction
First-level support skills for families and communities
Referral to qualified professionals
Culturally relevant health education for schools and churches

pillars.name: Disability Inclusion
pillars.outcome: Digital skills, assistive technology and remote-work pathways for persons with disabilities, anchored in Kirinyaga County.
pillars.lead: Disability is not inability. We work for a Kenya where every ability is valued, advocating for access, dignity and equal opportunity so that inclusion is lived, not just promised.
overview: This pillar rests on the belief that equal access to opportunity, especially in the growing digital economy, is a fundamental right. It tackles limited access to employment, digital exclusion and stigma directly.

Anchored in Kirinyaga County and designed to scale, we partner with specialised institutions and community service organisations to provide targeted digital skills, assistive technology and mentorship.
focus: Digital skills training designed for learners with disabilities
Assistive technology and the training to use it
Mentorship and remote-work readiness
Community awareness that challenges stigma

programmes.title: Digital skills and assistive technology
